questions.explanation: Option (A) value reconstructed. F = ma = 1500 × (-1.7) = -2550 N (A). The pasted options listed -2250 twice. Verify against the source.

An 8000 kg engine pulls a train of 5 wagons, each of 2000 kg, along a horizontal track. If the engine exerts a force of 40,000 N and the track offers a friction of 5000 N, then the net accelerating force acting on the system is:
questions.explanation: Net accelerating force = applied force − friction = 40,000 − 5000 = 35,000 N (C).

questions.body: A constant force acts on an object of mass 5 kg for a duration of 2 s. It increases the object's velocity from 3 m/s to 7 m/s. Find the magnitude of the applied force. If the same force were applied for a duration of 5 s, what would be the final velocity of the object?
Which would require a greater force — accelerating a 2 kg mass at 5 m/s² or a 4 kg mass at 2 m/s²?
questions.answer: F₁ = 2 × 5 = 10 N; F₂ = 4 × 2 = 8 N. Accelerating the 2 kg mass at 5 m/s² requires the greater force (10 N).
questions.explanation: Second mass reconstructed as '4 kg at 2 m/s²' (the paste was garbled as 'a kg mass at 2 m/s'). Verify against the source.

questions.body: A bullet of mass 20 g is fired horizontally with a velocity of 150 m/s from a pistol of mass 2 kg. What is the recoil velocity of the pistol?
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum: 0.02 × 150 = 2 × v → v = −1.5 m/s.

questions.body: A girl of mass 40 kg jumps with a horizontal velocity of 5 m/s onto a stationary cart with frictionless wheels. The mass of the cart is 3 kg. What is her velocity as the cart starts moving? Assume there is no external unbalanced force in the horizontal direction.

Two hockey players of opposite teams, while trying to hit a hockey ball on the ground, collide and immediately become entangled. One has a mass of 60 kg and was moving with a velocity of 5.0 m/s, while the other has a mass of 55 kg and was moving with a velocity of 6.0 m/s towards the first player. In which direction and with what velocity will they move after becoming entangled? Assume friction between the players' feet and the ground is negligible.
questions.explanation: Taking the first player's direction as positive: 60 × 5 − 55 × 6 = 300 − 330 = −30 kg·m/s; total mass = 115 kg; v = −30/115 = −0.26 m/s, i.e. in the direction the second (55 kg) player was moving.

questions.body: A body of mass 300 g is at rest. What force (in newton) must you apply to move it through 200 cm in 10 s?
questions.explanation: s = ½at² → 2 = ½·a·100 → a = 0.04 m/s²; F = 0.3 × 0.04 = 0.012 N. The pasted answer key ('0.12 m/s') is wrong in both value and unit — verify against the source.

questions.body: A boat of mass 3000 kg, initially at rest, is pulled by a force of 1.8 × 10⁴ N through a distance of 3 m. Assuming the resistance due to water is negligible, what is the velocity of the boat?

A 40 kg slab rests on a frictionless floor. A 10 kg block rests on top of the slab. The static coefficient of friction between the block and the slab is 0.60, while the kinetic coefficient is 0.40. The 10 kg block is acted upon by a horizontal force of 100 N. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², what is the resulting acceleration of the slab?
questions.explanation: The block slides, so the slab is driven only by kinetic friction: f = μk·m_block·g = 0.40 × 10 × 9.8 = 39.2 N; a_slab = f/m_slab = 39.2/40 = 0.98 m/s².

questions.body: A stone of mass 1 kg is thrown with a velocity of 20 m/s across the frozen surface of a lake and comes to rest after travelling a distance of 50 m. What is the force of friction between the stone and the ice?

An 8000 kg engine pulls a train of 5 wagons, each of 2000 kg, along a horizontal track. If the engine exerts a force of 40,000 N and the track offers a friction force of 5000 N, calculate: (a) the net accelerating force, (b) the acceleration of the train, and (c) the force of wagon 1 on wagon 2.
questions.answer: (a) Net accelerating force = 40,000 − 5000 = 35,000 N. (b) Acceleration of the train = 35,000 / 10,000 = 3.5 m/s² (taking the 5 wagons, 5 × 2000 = 10,000 kg, as the train being pulled). (c) Force of wagon 1 on wagon 2 = mass of wagons 2–5 × a = (4 × 2000) × 3.5 = 28,000 N.
questions.explanation: Matches the answer key (35,000 N; 3.5 m/s²; 28,000 N). Note the key computes acceleration from the wagons' mass (10,000 kg) only; including the engine (18,000 kg) would give 1.94 m/s². Confirm the intended interpretation.

questions.body: An automobile of mass 1500 kg is to be stopped with a negative acceleration of 1.7 m/s². What must be the force between the vehicle and the road?
questions.answer: F = ma = 1500 × 1.7 = 2550 N, directed opposite to the motion of the vehicle.

questions.body: What is the momentum of an object of mass m moving with a velocity v?

Two objects, each of mass 1.5 kg, are moving in the same straight line but in opposite directions. The velocity of each object is 2.5 m/s before the collision, during which they stick together. What will be the velocity of the combined object after the collision?
questions.explanation: Equal and opposite momenta cancel: 1.5 × 2.5 − 1.5 × 2.5 = 0; combined velocity = 0 m/s.

questions.body: A hockey ball of mass 200 g travelling at 10 m/s is struck by a hockey stick so as to return along its original path with a velocity of 5 m/s. Calculate the change of momentum that occurs in the motion of the hockey ball due to the force applied by the hockey stick.
questions.answer: Δp = m(v − u) = 0.2 × (−5 − 10) = −3 kg·m/s; magnitude = 3 kg·m/s, directed opposite to the original motion.

questions.body: A bullet of mass 100 g travelling horizontally with a velocity of 150 m/s strikes a stationary wooden block and comes to rest in 0.03 s. Calculate the distance of penetration of the bullet into the block. Also calculate the magnitude of the force exerted by the wooden block on the bullet.
questions.explanation: Distance 2.25 m matches the key. The pasted key states the force as '50 N', but F = 0.1 × 5000 = 500 N — likely a dropped zero. Verify against the source.

questions.body: An object of mass 1 kg travelling in a straight line with a velocity of 10 m/s collides with, and sticks to, a stationary wooden block of mass 5 kg. They then move off together in the same straight line. Calculate the total momentum just before and just after the impact, and the velocity of the combined object.
questions.answer: Momentum before = 1 × 10 = 10 kg·m/s; momentum after (conserved) = 10 kg·m/s; combined mass = 6 kg → velocity = 10/6 = 1.67 m/s.
questions.explanation: The pasted answer key gives the two momenta (10, 10 kg·m/s) but the final velocity value was missing; computed as 1.67 m/s. Verify against the source.

questions.body: An object of mass 100 kg is accelerated uniformly from a velocity of 5 m/s to 8 m/s in 6 s. Calculate the initial and final momentum of the object, and the magnitude of the force exerted on the object.

questions.body: How much momentum will a dumb-bell of mass 10 kg transfer to the floor if it falls from a height of 80 cm? Take its downward acceleration to be 10 m/s².
questions.explanation: v = √(2 × 10 × 0.8) = 4 m/s; momentum transferred = 10 × 4 = 40 kg·m/s.

questions.body: An object experiences a net zero external unbalanced force. Is it possible for the object to be travelling with a non-zero velocity? If yes, state the conditions that must be placed on the magnitude and direction of the velocity. If no, provide a reason.
questions.answer: Yes. By Newton's first law, with zero net force a body moves with constant velocity — so the velocity must be constant in both magnitude and direction (uniform motion in a straight line).

questions.body: When a carpet is beaten with a stick, dust comes out of it. Explain.
questions.answer: Beating suddenly sets the carpet in motion, but the dust particles, due to their inertia of rest, tend to remain in place. The carpet moves away while the dust stays behind, so it separates and falls out.

questions.body: Why is it advised to tie any luggage kept on the roof of a bus with a rope?
questions.answer: When the bus suddenly starts, stops or turns, the luggage tends to continue in its previous state of rest or motion due to inertia and may slide or fall off. The rope supplies the external force needed to keep it in place.

questions.body: Explain, with an example each, Newton's first, second and third laws of motion.
questions.answer: First law (law of inertia): a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an external force — e.g. passengers lurch forward when a moving bus brakes suddenly. Second law: the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, F = ma — e.g. a cricketer draws his hands back while catching a ball to increase the time of contact and reduce the force. Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction — e.g. the recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired, or a swimmer pushing water backward to move forward.
